If the politicians really want to help low and middle income

Yes.  Of course you can.


Scott Wagner (@ScottWagnerFL)

Miami-Dade: Residential homesteaded property tax is about ~$0.88 billion — just 6.9% of the $12.9 billion FY 2025‑26 budge. Removing it entirely leaves 12BB to spend: Miami-Dade last operated at less than 12BB in FY ‘23‑24. So you could eliminate completely and still operate at recent levels at 100% capacity.

Anyone claiming they care about making things more affordable for younger people should be enthusiastic about the proposal to alleviate the burden of property taxes.

The rest is just typical political blabber.  No more platitudes!


Brock Juarez (@Juarez_Brock)

The bottom line is for most millennials and Gen Z Americans—the next generation—homeownership is becoming out of reach. That’s a problem. 

Addressing the runaway train called property tax is an important first step. 

We should all tha

The Florida budget for next fiscal year (after line-item vetoes) will spend less than in the current fiscal year.

The budget for the current fiscal year spends less than the budget from the previous year, and that previous year’s budget spends less than the year before.

Four straight years of spending reductions!

2026 is not only the 250th anniversary of American independence, but also the 250th anniversary of the publication of Adam Smith’s highly influential Wealth of Nations, which represents a clarion call for economic independence from previously failed systems.
Yes it does.  Having a mortgage has no bearing on receiving the homestead exemption.

The FL Legislature passed a new congressional map that was sensible, thorough and justified in wake of changes in federal redistricting jurisprudence.  

It is not surprising that claims to the contrary have been rejected in court.

Local governments took in $32 billion in revenue from property taxes in 2019.

Today, that number is $60 billion.

Were services “collapsed” in 2019 when it was $32 billion?

OK, account for population growth and inflation in the ensuing years.  Still doesn’t get you anywhere near $60 billion.

There is no “collapse” in public services by phasing in an elimination of homestead property taxes, especially when starting the exemption at $250,000.


Vexly (@vexlyz)

Homestead tax wipe? Bold. Now fun

And that historic reduction is just the opening salvo.


Kyle Lamb (@kylamb8)

In 2025, the median value of a homestead property in Florida is ~338,000. With a current homestead exemption of $51,411, at 17 mills that same property would owe $4,872 annually. With a $250,000 exemption, the tax is reduced to $1,496. That's a 69% tax reduction at median value.



— https://nitter.net/kylamb8/status/2059751625355395296#m

Save Our Homes.  

Eliminate taxes on the homesteads of Florida residents!  

Special session on Monday to place in on the ballot.


Ron DeSantis (@GovRonDeSantis)

Today in Tampa, I outlined the Save Our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes plan that will eliminate taxes on homesteads. 

Property tax revenue collected by local governments has nearly doubled in the past seven years (from $32 billion to $60 billion) and is expected to reach an astounding $83 billion by 2032.

If only DC could follow our model.

Make merit great again!


Neetu Arnold (@neetu_arnold)

University of California STEM professors want standardized tests back due to severe math deficiencies among students:

“We now observe preparation gaps so severe that instructors must reteach middle school mathematics”

“The current admissions metric, based primarily on GPA & essays, can no longer reliably distinguish readiness for university-level STEM majors in an era of severe grade inflation & AI assisted application essays”







— ht

You‘re not the only one!


Tracy Beanz (@tracybeanz)

This is what should be happening EVERYWHERE. If you have to pay taxes, you don't own your home. I can not WAIT to vote for this.

Correct!


Michelle Weekley (@michelleweekley)

The key here is that this applies to Homestead properties which are full time primary residences, not just boomers. 

The free state of Florida is about to be a little more free!

Exactly.


Alex Nitzberg (@alexnitzberg)

While I'm not a senior, my property taxes are folded into my mortgage payments, so if those property taxes were reduced to $0, my monthly mortgage payment would decrease.
